newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Abbey National hopeful about Hong Kong prospects. [CORRECTED 14:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Abbey National hopeful about Hong Kong prospects. [CORRECTED 14:10 GMT]

text.p: Abbey National Plc said on Friday that it saw Hong Kong-based business playing a significant role in its future activities.

The bank's chairman Lord Tugendhat told Reuters in an interview that while Abbey National's involvement in the region was currently quite small compared to its overall operations, it would be important for the future.
"Things have moved quite rapidly. We have been doing a lot of business in this part of the world with governments, with bond issues," he said.
The bank has been doing retail business too and will shortly start up a joint venture international private banking operation with Dah Sing and Hambros Plc, he said.
"The scope for capital flows in this region is simply immense," said Gareth Jones, the bank's managing director of treasury and wholesale banking.
(Corrects to give Jones' full name and title).
"There are huge infrastructure projects at the same time there are huge savings," he added.
"There is a huge vibrancy about this place and in the run up to June 30 (when Hong Kong is to return to Chinese from British rule) it has intensified."
Abbey National set up a representative office in Hong Kong about 18 months ago and earlier this year took a five percent stake in Hong Kong banking group Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd .
"I think that has been seen as a vote of confidence in Hong Kong's future as an international financial entrepot as well as the gateway to China," Tugendhat said.
"Organisations like us have to live with change and seek to profit by it." -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6345
